"A mountain doesn't move -- but it's still there when the storm's gone. Summit a tower. Win five bouts. Then go to the Dragon's Ribs, where the dragon's heart is, and stand in front of what lives there. Come back and tell me what you'll be."

"All rivers come back to the sea. Climb a tower to its top. Win five bouts without anger. Then go to the Tidewrecked Court, where the flood began, and end it. Come back and tell me where you'll flow next."

"I have kept this monastery sixty years believing the Heart of the Deep is holy. A brother came back from the Cooling Dunes and said it is only hungry. Bring me what he saw: the carving at the dune's heart."

"I'm older than the trees, I said. Not older than what's below. Summit a tower. Read five of the old stones. Then go to the Rotting Bloom, where the hunger started, and end it for good. Then tell me what you'll keep."
"Our order keeps silence because the Deep listens. Seven silent bells hold the Hollow Moon together. Someone has been ringing them. Find them in the Thawed Archive and still them."

"The pages say the first abbot carried a mirror that showed the moon even underground -- and that something below ate the moon out of it. It's in the Starless Pit. Bring it back, and the monastery will have its moon again."

"The willow bends -- but our creed also says the storm prunes the weak. I've taught you to bend. Now learn to be the storm. Summit a tower. Win five bouts. And go down to the Black Canopy, where the rot began."

Before Eliet, the world had two great powers. In the cities of the High Age, machines did the work of gods. In the hills of the Old Way, cultivators did it with breath and will. Each side thought the other a plague.

It stopped when both sides were out of everything but each other. A machine-wright and a sect elder sat down in the ruins. Each had learned the same hard thing. Machines without qi were cold. Qi without craft was slow. Alone, neither could win. Together, they could stand.
The Heart is not a mind. It is a scale. It weighs the two roads in whoever stands before it. Once it hung level. Now it leans, and the whole deep leans with it. That is why the floors grow hard.

The builders put the five elements into the deep as a cycle. Each one feeds the next, and each one checks another. A clash is not an enemy. If all five are strong, a clash only makes the bonds around it stronger.
The deep is the thing they built. Mo calls it the Accord's school. It is no prison and no monster. It tests whoever comes down, and it teaches by taking away whatever you lean on too hard.

The nanites are the machine half of the Accord. Qi is the other half. A child of Eliet carries one half in the blood, and the deep waits for them to find the other. The ladder to the heavens never reached because a ladder is only half a bridge.

The old stones say the deep is kind to anyone who holds both roads. Walk only the machine road, and your qi sours. Walk only the sitting road, and the heat finds you. Keep to the middle, and the deep gets out of your way.

The peace held two thousand years. Then people forgot why. They split the Accord into parts and sold the parts. The deep was left alone, and it kept on teaching in its own way. It grew dark, because no one came down to learn.

They called the peace the Balance. A cultivator's breath would steady a machine's hand. A machine's reach would carry a cultivator's will. Both ages swore to build one thing together, so that neither could ever go to war alone again.

They fought for three hundred years. Qi fire burned the cities. Machine plague emptied the sects. Nobody won. The hills around Eliet were one of the battlefields, and the jade the first families dug is part of what was left.

Those who reach the bottom in balance say the last floors were quiet. The Heart takes the one who leans, and lets the one who stands level walk through. That is the secret the builders hid in the deep, and it is the only one.
